headline: Zero tolerance for 'crossfire', IGP’s remarks were inappropriate: Home Minister

members.title: Zero tolerance for 'crossfire', IGP’s remarks were inappropriate: Home Minister
members.lead: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has directly rejected Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir’s remarks on “crossfire”, saying the government does not want such incidents and has a zero-tolerance policy towards them. “The government does not want crossfire; rather, it has zero tolerance for crossfire,” the home minister said. Describing the IGP’s remarks as inadvertent, he added, “That was not right. He should not have said that.” At an event in Chawkbazar in Old Dhaka on Monday, IGP Md Ali Hossain Fakir said the police would resort to “crossfire” if necessary, provided the government gave permission. He said that when the police used force, one side called them fascists, while when they remained inactive, they were branded weak. The police must be given an appropriate environment to carry out their duties and maintain law and order, he added. .Why the IGP’s mention of ‘crossfire’ is alarming. Asked about the remarks on Tuesday evening, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told Prothom Alo, “He (the IGP) is a straightforward person. While speaking about the strict enforcement of the law, he made the remark inadvertently. That was not right. He should not have said that.” . The home minister firmly reiterated that the government did not want crossfire and maintained a zero-tolerance policy towards it. He said the government would not allow extrajudicial killings and would take an extremely firm stance on the issue. The government would not tolerate extrajudicial killings or custodial deaths, he added. .Police headquarters clarifies IGP’s remarks on ‘crossfire’. Salahuddin Ahmed said the rule of law was the government’s principal objective, while improving law and order was its top priority. No deaths in crossfire or in custody had occurred so far, he said. However, the government would take all necessary measures to curb crime and ensure the proper enforcement of the law. members.title: Why is the police chief talking about ‘crossfire’ killings?
members.lead: Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir’s remark, “If the government gives permission, we will carry out crossfire killings,” has sparked concern and controversy. Questions have been raised about extrajudicial killings, human rights and accountability within the police force. Watch the video for details.
